literal: Ju pointed at Xiuyi and said, "The man in this seat defies the Son of Heaven's clear edict—'whoever amasses the most goods gets office'—while daylight robbery runs riot in the capital. Is he not a great thief?"
idiomatic: Ju pointed at Xiuyi and said, "The man in this seat defies the Son of Heaven's clear edict—'whoever amasses the most goods gets office'—while daylight robbery runs riot in the capital. Is he not a great thief?"

literal: Xiuyi turned pale.
idiomatic: Xiuyi turned pale.

literal: Ju stormed out cursing; afterward he wished to intercept the imperial carriage and plead Xiuyi's crimes, but Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin persuaded him to desist.
idiomatic: Ju stormed out cursing. Later he wished to waylay the imperial carriage and plead Xiuyi's crimes, but Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin talked him out of it.

literal: When the two Qins rebelled, Xiuyi was made acting Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Western Route Mobile Office, and acting governor of Qinzhou, with command over all armies.
idiomatic: When the two Qins rebelled, Xiuyi was made acting Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Western Route Mobile Office, and acting governor of Qinzhou, with command over all armies.

literal: Xiuyi loved wine and drank for days on end; he then fell ill with wind disorder, his mind clouded—though he reached Chang'an, he accomplished nothing in organizing the defense.
idiomatic: Xiuyi loved wine and drank for days on end, then fell ill with wind disorder and lost his wits. Though he reached Chang'an, he did nothing to organize the defense.

literal: Yuan Zhi was defeated and lost; the rebels advanced east to Heishui. Xiao Baoyin was again sent to suppress them, with Xiuyi as governor of Yongzhou.
idiomatic: Yuan Zhi was defeated and lost; the rebels advanced east to Heishui. Xiao Baoyin was again sent against them, with Xiuyi as governor of Yongzhou.

literal: He died in the province; posthumously made Minister of Works, posthumous name Wen.
idiomatic: He died in the province and was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous name Wen.

literal: His son Jun rose to Attendant Cadet at the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: His son Jun rose to Attendant Cadet at the Yellow Gate.

literal: Later he entered Western Wei, was enfeoffed Prince of Anchang, and held the post of Grand Guardian of the Palace with nominal equal ritual to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: Later he entered Western Wei, was enfeoffed Prince of Anchang, and held the post of Grand Guardian of the Palace with nominal equal ritual to the Three Excellencies.

literal: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works, posthumous name Ping.
idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous name Ping.

literal: His son Ze, styled Xiaogui, inherited the title and held the post of governor of Yizhou.
idiomatic: His son Ze, styled Xiaogui, inherited the title and served as governor of Yizhou.

literal: In Zhou he served as Junior Household Steward and governor-general of Jiangling.
idiomatic: In Zhou he served as Junior Household Steward and governor-general of Jiangling.

literal: Before long Yuwen Huaji installed Prince Hao of Qin as emperor and marched with troops to Pengcheng; everywhere trembled at the news.
idiomatic: Before long Yuwen Huaji installed Prince Hao of Qin as emperor and marched on Pengcheng; the land shook at the news.

literal: Wendu urged Tong to send envoys to Li Mi.
idiomatic: Wendu urged Tong to send envoys to Li Mi.

literal: Mi then offered surrender; they conferred office and rank on him and treated his envoys with great courtesy.
idiomatic: Mi then offered surrender; they conferred office and rank on him and treated his envoys with great courtesy.

literal: Wang Shichong was displeased; Wendu knew it and secretly planned to kill Shichong.
idiomatic: Wang Shichong was displeased; Wendu knew it and secretly planned to kill Shichong.

literal: Tong made Wendu Inspector of the Masters of Writing, but Shichong firmly blocked it.
idiomatic: Tong made Wendu Inspector of the Masters of Writing, but Shichong firmly blocked it.

literal: Lu Chu urged Wendu to kill him; Wendu then entered the hall with a memorial in his breast.
idiomatic: Lu Chu urged Wendu to kill him; Wendu then entered the hall with a memorial hidden in his robe.

literal: Someone informed Shichong; he galloped back to Hanjia Fortress.
idiomatic: Someone informed Shichong; he galloped back to Hanjia Fortress.

literal: At night rebellion broke out; they attacked the East Gate of the Sun and entered, bowing below Ziwei Watchtower and saying, "We ask to execute Wendu and lay the guilt on the Minister of Justice."
idiomatic: At night rebellion broke out. They attacked the East Gate of the Sun and entered, bowing below Ziwei Watchtower and saying, "We ask to execute Wendu and lay the guilt on the Minister of Justice."

literal: Tong saw the troops were strong and sent his appointed general Huang Taoshu to seize Wendu and bring him out.
idiomatic: Tong saw the troops were strong and sent his appointed general Huang Taoshu to seize Wendu and bring him out.

literal: Wendu turned to Tong and said, "I die at dawn; Your Majesty will follow at dusk."
idiomatic: Wendu turned to Tong and said, "I die at dawn; Your Majesty will follow at dusk."

literal: Tong wept as he sent him away; none on left or right could speak for grief.
idiomatic: Tong wept as he sent him away; none on left or right could speak for grief.

literal: Outside Xingjiao Gate Shichong ordered his attendants to hack Wendu to pieces; all his sons were also killed.
idiomatic: Outside Xingjiao Gate Shichong ordered his attendants to hack Wendu to pieces; all his sons were also killed.

literal: Ze's younger brother Ju, styled Xiaoju—in Western Wei he inherited his grandfather's title Marquis of Shiping county and was appointed governor of Nanfeng.
idiomatic: Ze's younger brother Ju, styled Xiaoju—in Western Wei he inherited his grandfather's title as Marquis of Shiping county and was appointed governor of Nanfeng.

literal: Seeing the Yuan house would fall, he secretly told his brothers, "The heart of the Yuwen clan is plain to every passerby."
idiomatic: Seeing the Yuan house would fall, he secretly told his brothers, "The heart of the Yuwen clan is plain to every passerby."

literal: "When the roof totters yet none props it up, of what use are clan sons!"
idiomatic: "When the roof totters yet none props it up, of what use are clan sons!"

literal: His elder brother Ze stopped him, and he desisted.
idiomatic: His elder brother Ze stopped him, and he desisted.

literal: Later Zhou Wendi married his sister to his nephew Duke Jin of Jin Gao Hu; their bond was very close.
idiomatic: Later Zhou Wendi married his sister to his nephew Duke Jin of Jin, Gao Hu; their bond was very close.

literal: When Hu was executed, he was banished to Shu for guilt by association.
idiomatic: When Hu was executed, he was banished to Shu for guilt by association.

literal: Later appointed Minister of Law in the Ministry of Justice.
idiomatic: Later he was appointed Minister of Law in the Ministry of Justice.

literal: Emperor Wen of Sui valued his lineage and married his daughter to the Princess of Fangling.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui valued his lineage and married his daughter to the Princess of Fangling.

literal: When Wen became Chancellor, he appointed Xiaoju Junior Household Steward, ranked as Pillar of State, enfeoffed Marquis of Xunyang commandery.
idiomatic: When Wen became Chancellor, he appointed Xiaoju Junior Household Steward, ranked him Pillar of State, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xunyang commandery.

literal: When Fangling was established as crown prince, his daughter was made crown princess; favors grew heavier, and he was made governor-general of Shouzhou.
idiomatic: When Fangling was established as crown prince, his daughter was made crown princess. Favors grew heavier, and he was made governor-general of Shouzhou.

literal: When Chen generals Ren Mannu and others repeatedly raided north of the river, Xiaoju was again made overall commander of the field army and camped troops on the river.
idiomatic: When Chen generals Ren Mannu and others repeatedly raided north of the river, Xiaoju was again made overall commander of the field army and camped troops on the river.

literal: Later, in old age, he memorialized begging leave to retire.
idiomatic: Later, in old age, he memorialized begging leave to retire.

literal: He was made governor of Jingzhou.
idiomatic: He was made governor of Jingzhou.

literal: He died in office; posthumous name Jian.
idiomatic: He died in office; posthumous name Jian.

literal: His son Wujie inherited.
idiomatic: His son Wujie inherited.

literal: Ju's next younger brother Ya, styled Xiaofang, had civil and military talent.
idiomatic: Ju's next younger brother Ya, styled Xiaofang, had civil and military talent.

literal: In Kaihuang he served as Left Leader of the Palace Guard Left and Right, governor of Ji and Qin prefectures, enfeoffed Duke of Shunyang commandery.
idiomatic: In Kaihuang he served as Left Leader of the Palace Guards, governor of Ji and Qin prefectures, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Shunyang commandery.

literal: Ya's younger brother Bao, styled Xiaozheng, from youth had the measure of a grown man.
idiomatic: Ya's younger brother Bao, styled Xiaozheng, from youth had the measure of a grown man.

literal: Orphaned at ten, he was cherished and raised by all his elder brothers.
idiomatic: Orphaned at ten, he was cherished and raised by all his elder brothers.

literal: He was good to all his elder brothers.
idiomatic: He was good to all his elder brothers.

literal: When the brothers debated separate households, Bao wept and remonstrated; they would not listen.
idiomatic: When the brothers debated separate households, Bao wept and remonstrated; they would not listen.

literal: The family was rich in gold and treasure; Bao took none of it and walked out alone.
idiomatic: The family was rich in gold and treasure; Bao took none of it and walked out alone.

literal: In Zhou he held the post of Grand Guardian of the Palace, Marquis of Beiping county, governor of Zhaozhou.
idiomatic: In Zhou he held the post of Grand Guardian of the Palace, was Marquis of Beiping county, and governor of Zhaozhou.

literal: Following Wei Xiaokuan he pacified Yu Chi Tong's rebellion; for merit he was made Pillar of State and advanced to Duke of Hejian commandery.
idiomatic: Following Wei Xiaokuan he pacified Yu Chi Tong's rebellion; for merit he was made Pillar of State and advanced to Duke of Hejian commandery.

literal: In Sui Kaihuang he was made governor-general of Yuanzhou.
idiomatic: In Sui Kaihuang he was made governor-general of Yuanzhou.

literal: A merchant was robbed by bandits; the man suspected his fellow lodger and seized him.
idiomatic: A merchant was robbed by bandits; the man suspected his fellow lodger and seized him.

literal: Bao saw his expression was wronged yet his words were upright, and released him.
idiomatic: Bao saw his expression was wronged yet his words were upright, and released him.

literal: The merchant went to court accusing Bao of taking gold and letting the thief go.
idiomatic: The merchant went to court accusing Bao of taking gold and letting the thief go.

literal: Emperor Wen of Sui sent men to investigate thoroughly; the envoy rebuked Bao in the register—why take gold and release the robber?
idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui sent men to investigate thoroughly; the envoy rebuked Bao in the register—why take gold and release the robber?

literal: Bao accepted blame without dissent.
idiomatic: Bao accepted blame without dissent.

literal: The envoy went to the capital together with Bao, and he was dismissed from office.
idiomatic: The envoy went to the capital together with Bao, and he was dismissed from office.

literal: The real robber was soon exposed elsewhere.
idiomatic: The real robber was soon exposed elsewhere.

literal: The emperor said, "Why go so far as to false-accuse yourself?"
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Why go so far as to false-accuse yourself?"

literal: Bao said, "I was entrusted with one province and could not quell robbery—that is my first fault;
idiomatic: Bao said, "I was entrusted with one province and could not quell robbery—that is my first fault;

literal: a commoner was slandered, yet I did not hand him to the law courts and at once set him free—that is my second fault;
idiomatic: a commoner was slandered, yet I did not hand him to the law courts and at once set him free—that is my second fault;

literal: I ignored how things would look and to this day am suspected by others—that is my third fault.
idiomatic: I ignored how things would look and to this day am suspected by others—that is my third fault.

literal: I have three faults—how escape punishment!
idiomatic: I have three faults—how can I escape punishment!

literal: If I did not say I had taken bribes, the envoy would press further in investigation; then bonds and fetters would fall on the innocent, doubling a great minister's fault—that is why I falsely accused myself."
idiomatic: If I did not say I had taken bribes, the envoy would press further in investigation; then bonds and fetters would fall on the innocent, doubling a great minister's fault—that is why I falsely accused myself."

literal: The emperor sighed in wonder and called him an elder of virtue.
idiomatic: The emperor sighed in wonder and called him an elder of virtue.

literal: Prince of Leliang Wanshou—enfeoffed in the third year of Heping, made Grand General Conquering the East, garrisoned Helong.
idiomatic: Prince of Leliang Wanshou was enfeoffed in the third year of Heping, made Grand General Conquering the East, and garrisoned Helong.

literal: Greedy and violent by nature; on the return march he died of anxiety on the road; posthumous name Prince Li.
idiomatic: Greedy and violent by nature, on the return march he died of anxiety on the road; posthumous name Prince Li.

literal: His son Prince of Kang Le Ping succeeded.
idiomatic: His son, Prince of Kang Le Ping, succeeded.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Changming inherited.
idiomatic: His son Changming inherited.

literal: For killing a man he was sentenced to death and the fief was abolished.
idiomatic: For killing a man he was sentenced to death and the fief was abolished.

literal: His son Zhong—in Emperor Ming's time the former title was restored, post of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
idiomatic: His son Zhong—in Emperor Ming's time the former title was restored; he held the post of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

literal: Emperor Xiaowu went boating on the Tianquan Pool and ordered princes of the imperial clan to attend the feast.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu went boating on the Tianquan Pool and ordered princes of the imperial clan to attend the feast.

literal: Zhong was stupid and witless, loved clothes by nature, and wore a red gauze jacket with embroidered collar, green silk trousers with brocade trim.
idiomatic: Zhong was stupid and witless, loved clothes by nature, and wore a red gauze jacket with embroidered collar and green silk trousers with brocade trim.

literal: The emperor said to him, "Court dress ought to have a fixed form—why wear the costume of street performers?"
idiomatic: The emperor said to him, "Court dress ought to have a fixed form—why wear the costume of street performers?"

literal: Zhong said, "What I have loved since youth lives in brocades and gauzes; song robes and dance garments are my heart's wish."
idiomatic: Zhong said, "What I have loved since youth lives in brocades and gauzes; song robes and dance garments are my heart's wish."

literal: The emperor said, "Can a man be so devoid of conscience?"
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Can a man be so devoid of conscience?"

literal: Prince of Guangping Luohou—enfeoffed second year of Heping.
idiomatic: Prince of Guangping Luohou was enfeoffed in the second year of Heping.

literal: He died; posthumous name Prince Shang.
idiomatic: He died; posthumous name Prince Shang.

literal: He had no son; later the fifth son of Prince of Yangping the Somber was made his heir.
idiomatic: He had no son; later the fifth son of Prince of Yangping the Somber was made his heir.

literal: Kuang styled Jianfu, nature upright and unyielding, with spirit and integrity.
idiomatic: Kuang, styled Jianfu, was upright and unyielding, with spirit and integrity.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen prized him.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen prized him.

literal: He said to him, "Uncle, you can be the model for the altars of state and support my person; you may now change your name to Kuang, to complete the beauty of a loyal end."
idiomatic: He said to him, "Uncle, you can be the model for the altars of state and support my person. You may now change your name to Kuang, to complete the beauty of a loyal end."

literal: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant at the Yellow Gate.

literal: Ru Hao first won favor; all officials slightly feared him.
idiomatic: Ru Hao first won favor; all officials slightly feared him.

literal: Once when the emperor was returning from the imperial tombs he ordered Kuang to share the carriage and also had Hao mount.
idiomatic: Once when the emperor was returning from the imperial tombs he ordered Kuang to share the carriage and also had Hao mount.

literal: Hao lifted his robe to climb; Kuang remonstrated; the emperor pushed him down. Hao hated Kuang and turned pale.
idiomatic: Hao lifted his robe to climb; Kuang remonstrated; the emperor pushed him down. Hao hated Kuang and turned pale.

literal: At the time men admired his forthright loyalty.
idiomatic: At the time men admired his forthright loyalty.

literal: When Xuanwu personally held government, he was appointed governor of Sizhou.
idiomatic: When Xuanwu personally held government, he was appointed governor of Sizhou.

literal: Kuang had already crossed Hao and feared harm; he cultivated integrity and caution, winning a strong reputation.
idiomatic: Kuang had already crossed Hao and feared harm; he cultivated integrity and caution and won a strong reputation.

literal: He was transferred to governor of Hengzhou.
idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Hengzhou.

literal: He was summoned as Grand Master of the Imperial Clan and chief rectifier of the Henan fief.
idiomatic: He was summoned as Grand Master of the Imperial Clan and chief rectifier of the Henan fief.

literal: Kuang memorialized that wives of imperial princes and of first- and second-rank princes should all bear the title consort.
idiomatic: Kuang memorialized that wives of imperial princes and of first- and second-rank princes should all bear the title consort.

literal: But third-rank princes and below all called theirs "wife."
idiomatic: But third-rank princes and below all called theirs "wife."

literal: Above they could not share the same consort title as imperial consorts, yet below they fell short of the titled ladies given fifth rank and above—he humbly felt this doubtful.
idiomatic: Above they could not share the consort title of imperial consorts, yet below they fell short of the titled ladies of fifth rank and above—he felt this doubtful.

literal: The edict said, "Honor in court, glory in the chamber; women have no fixed rank but rise with their husbands.
idiomatic: The edict said, "Honor in court, glory in the chamber; women have no fixed rank but rise with their husbands.

literal: Third-rank princes have opened princely fiefs; consort titles ought likewise to be equal.
idiomatic: Third-rank princes have opened princely fiefs; consort titles ought likewise to be equal.

literal: "Wife" means "equal"—in principle equal to oneself; they may follow the consort precedent.
idiomatic: "Wife" means "equal"—in principle equal to oneself; they may follow the consort precedent.

literal: From then the titles for wives of third-rank princes were fixed.
idiomatic: From then the titles for wives of third-rank princes were fixed.

literal: Soon he was removed and made Minister of Revenue.
idiomatic: Soon he was removed and made Minister of Revenue.

literal: Kuang memorialized citing precedents of Leling and Zhangwu, seeking to inherit Luohou's fief.
idiomatic: Kuang memorialized citing precedents of Leling and Zhangwu, seeking to inherit Luohou's fief.

literal: An edict referred it to the Masters of Writing for deliberation.
idiomatic: An edict referred it to the Masters of Writing for deliberation.
